notes.executionRules: The 'Shared execution rules' in the index impl-plans/active/search-engine-adapter.md are binding. All workers run on branch main in one working directory. Workers run no git write commands and create no worktrees or branches. Before each edit, fresh-read the file and record its shasum -a 256; record the post-edit hash in the worker's own plan Progress Log. Copy the plan to tmp/search-engine-adapter/<P#>/plan-snapshot.md as an immutable intent snapshot before the first edit. Edit only your own writePaths. sharedPaths are read-only unless a sharedPathNotes entry grants a specific edit. Never touch .riela/, the index (P11 excepted), other plans' files or lockfiles. Run no broad formatters.
notes.evidenceLayout: Evidence lives under the untracked, gitignored evidenceRoot tmp/search-engine-adapter, with one subdirectory per plan short id (P1..P11). A re-run writes into tmp/search-engine-adapter/<P#>/attempt-<n>/ and keeps earlier logs. Run mkdir -p first, because tee does not create directories.
notes.shell: Verification commands use the bash-only ${PIPESTATUS[0]}, so they are wrapped in bash -c. A blank exit= is not evidence. Swift tests need PKG_CONFIG_PATH=$PWD/.build/anydoc-native/host/pkgconfig. Run mise run build once first. bun is reachable only through mise exec or mise run.
notes.peerBreaks: Concurrent workers in a wave share one .build. A compile failure in a file outside your writePaths that belongs to another in-flight plan is not yours to edit. Retry up to 3 times, about 2 minutes apart. After that, record 'blocked by peer <planId>' (never 'passed'); P11 re-runs it.
notes.fileOwnership: Sources/AppCore/NoteService.swift has one owner per wave: P2 (wave 1, the deleteNoteRows enqueue line) and P5 (wave 2, the searchEngine stored property). Sources/AppCore/KaibaConfiguration.swift is owned only by P1. mise.toml is owned only by P10. README.md is owned only by P11.
notes.commitPolicy: AGENTS.md governs commits: no emojis, no machine-local absolute paths, no secrets, and no AI attribution in commit messages. .riela/ stays untracked and is never committed; tmp/ is gitignored. Workers do not commit. P11 does not commit, push or archive plans; workflow finalization owns that.
notes.dockerPolicy: P10 and P11 need Docker (colima) for search:up and search:test-live. If it is unavailable, record 'blocked: docker unavailable' with the exact error. Never record it as passed.

reviewContext.issueReference: No GitHub issue. Inline workflowInput 'Optional search-engine adapter: full-text search and related-notes search (Elasticsearch first, local docker compose)' (workflow opus-luna-design-and-implement-review-loop-session-262; design accepted in comm-003677).
reviewContext.userProblem: kaiba searches only with SQLite FTS5. The user wants an optional external search engine (Elasticsearch first) for full-text search and related-notes search for the open note. It must be active only when configured, keep the existing behavior otherwise, never fail writes, and never leak notes across libraries or users.
requiredOutcomes: SE1: an AppCore SearchEngine protocol and value types, a factory, and NoteService.searchEngine.
SE2: an optional searchEngine config section with credentials only as environment-variable names; an unknown kind is a clear error.

SE3: a durable gated outbox at store v23, hooked at refreshFTS, deleteNoteRows, moveNotebook and the tag-memo rehome. Activation backfills. Claim and settle use a lease and a generation counter, with retry backoff capped at 1 hour.
SE4: an engine filter built from NoteSearchScope plus a store re-check using the searchNotes predicates; relatedNotes requires a readable source and excludes it.
SE5: GraphQL searchEngineCapability, engineSearchNotes and relatedNotes, with the statuses feature-disabled and search-engine-unavailable, plus KaibaClient operations.
SE7: web capability flag, engine-backed grep search with fallback, and a Related notes section in the Links tab.
SE8: an Elasticsearch 8.x adapter over URLSession with a cjk analyzer, strict mapping, bulk NDJSON and sanitized errors.
SE9: docker/elasticsearch/compose.yaml, mise search:* tasks and an env-gated live test.
nonGoals: Other engines, embeddings or vector search, and feeding engine hits into FTS fusion.
Changing searchNotes, NoteSearchPopup or the agent search_notes tool.
A GraphQL admin reindex, index aliases, and automatic deletion of old indices.
A kuromoji analyzer or a detach command (open user-qa questions).
constraints: No behavior change when unconfigured; no new required dependency.
Never fail or roll back writes because of the engine; no engine call inside a store transaction.
Access enforced in the engine filter AND by a store re-check.
Swift files under 1000 lines; swiftlint; existing SwiftPM targets; URLSession only.
No secrets or absolute local paths in code, docs or logs; credentials by environment-variable name.
Run web:check and tauri:check because web/ changes.
designDecisionsAndRationale: The outbox is hooked at the existing refreshFTS and deleteNoteRows choke points plus the two notebook library updates, so every indexed-field change is captured atomically.
The enqueue is gated by EXISTS(search_engine_sync_state), so never-activated stores write nothing.
The outbox tables are created before requireSupportedVersion, because upgradeToVersion22 calls refreshFTS.
Engine search is a separate GraphQL field, so the default path and BM25 rank semantics are untouched.
relatedNotes uses like-text from the store, so it does not depend on index lag.
Plain http is allowed only for loopback hosts; the compose file binds to 127.0.0.1.
supportedEdgeCases: Engine down: writes commit, rows back off, the server starts anyway, and the web falls back to built-in search.
Index identity change (prefix or mapping version): full backfill on activation.
Note deleted before the push: a delete is pushed. Orphaned documents are dropped by the re-check.
A write racing a push: the generation counter keeps the row for re-push.
Caller with no reachable libraries: empty result, no engine call.
An older server without the new fields: the web treats the capability as false.
residualRisksFromDesignReview: A stale engine tag_ids value affects relevance only, never access.
The activation backfill upsert needs WHERE true (pinned in P2).
The ES image tag is verified at implementation time (P10).
Deactivated stores keep enqueueing, bounded at one row per note.
intentionalTradeoffs: Durable outbox at store v23 instead of best-effort pushes: one extra gated statement per note write in exchange for no lost index updates; an engine outage only delays indexing.
Engine search is a separate GraphQL field (engineSearchNotes), not a searchNotes mode: clients choose the path explicitly, and BM25 ranks stay separate from engine scores.
Built-in cjk bigram analyzer instead of kuromoji: works on the stock Elasticsearch image with no plugins, at the cost of weaker Japanese morphology.
Reindex/backfill is CLI-only (kaiba search-engine sync|reindex, store administrator) plus automatic server backfill on activation or index identity change; no GraphQL admin mutation.
KaibaClient operations are hand-written in the existing KaibaOperations.swift style, not generated.
Plain http is accepted only for loopback hosts, with no override flag; the local compose cluster runs with xpack.security.enabled=false bound to 127.0.0.1 and is documented as local-only.
Deactivated stores keep enqueueing, bounded at one outbox row per note, until the engine is re-enabled.
P7 lives in Sources/AppCore/CommandSearchEngine.swift with --output json|text (existing CLI convention and testable target) instead of the design-named AppCLI file with --json; behavior unchanged.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Engines other than Elasticsearch 8.x, and vector or embedding search.
Feeding engine hits into the FTS lexical fusion ranking.
Engine-backed NoteSearchPopup link picker and agent search_notes tool (both stay on FTS).
Index aliases and automatic deletion of old indices after an index identity change.
A kaiba search-engine detach command to clear the activation marker and outbox (open user-qa question).
Optional kuromoji analyzer selection (open user-qa question).
Non-loopback plain http engine URLs, for example a LAN cluster without TLS (open user-qa question).
